title: Multivariate Long-term Profile Monitoring with Application to the KW51 Railway Bridge
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures, conference. arXiv admin note: text overlap with arXiv:2408.02106
abstract: Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) plays a pivotal role in modern civil engineering, providing critical insights into the health and integrity of infrastructure systems. This work presents a novel multivariate long-term profile monitoring approach to eliminate fluctuations in the measured response quantities, e.g., caused by environmental influences or measurement error. Our methodology addresses critical challenges in SHM and combines supervised methods with unsupervised, principal component analysis-based approaches in a single overarching framework, offering both flexibility and robustness in handling real-world large and/or sparse sensor data streams. We propose a function-on-function regression framework, which leverages functional data analysis for multivariate sensor data and integrates nonlinear modeling techniques, mitigating covariate-induced variations that can obscure structural changes.
